props.title: Jurassic Park

sections.content: Jurassic Park revolutionized blockbuster filmmaking by seamlessly blending practical effects and CGI. Spielberg's masterful direction creates unbearable tension - the T-Rex attack remains a masterclass in sustained suspense, while the kitchen velociraptor scene proves less-is-more horror works best. The film's groundbreaking visual effects by ILM hold up remarkably well today, especially compared to Terminator 2 (1991) and other early CGI films. The practical animatronics by Stan Winston's team gave the dinosaurs weight and presence that pure CGI still struggles to match.

sections.content: The film's influence extends far beyond its technical achievements. Deep Blue Sea (1999), Anaconda (1997), and Lake Placid (1999) all attempted to recreate Jurassic Park's blend of creature feature thrills and cutting-edge effects. But none matched Spielberg's perfect pacing and character work. The film's themes of scientific ethics and human hubris inspired thoughtful sci-fi like Ex Machina (2014) and Splice (2009).

Michael Crichton's techno-thriller template - scientific breakthrough goes wrong - influenced countless films like Rise of the Planet of the Apes (2011) and Deep Blue Sea (1999). But Jurassic Park succeeds by making its characters compelling beyond their function in the plot. Sam Neill's Alan Grant has a complete arc about accepting children that pays off organically through the story. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Modern Monster Movies

movies.title: Jaws
movies.slug: Spielberg's first blockbuster monster movie proves his mastery of tension and reveal

sections.content: Modern monster films still reference Jurassic Park's innovations. Cloverfield (2008) uses similar reveal techniques, hiding its creature until the perfect moment. Pacific Rim (2013) channels the same sense of awe at massive scale. Even non-monster movies like Gravity (2013) learned from its groundbreaking CGI integration. The original film's practical-digital hybrid approach influenced Mad Max: Fury Road (2015) and The Force Awakens (2015).
